title: Protocols for evaluating local bacterial viscoelastic environment and mechanical coupling in dilute bacterial suspensions
protocol: Reactivate stored bacterial strain by culturing on appropriate solid medium at optimal growth conditions.
Prepare overnight stationary phase culture in appropriate liquid medium at optimal conditions.
Transfer 1% (v/v) of overnight culture to 20 ml of fresh medium for determining bacterial mechanical coupling.
Incubate bacterial culture at optimal conditions until early exponential phase.
Put the culture on ice prior to optical tweezers experiments.
Optional: Inoculate 20 ml of fresh medium with 1% (v/v) of culture in an early exponential phase and incubate until early exponential phase is reached again.
Repeat optional step using regrown early exponential culture for optical tweezers experiments.
Calibrate optical tweezers by recording bead position fluctuations in a stationary trap.
Record at least 30,000 frames during each calibration run.
Determine bead positions using particle tracking software PartTrack V3.36 for Aresis Tweezer.
Fit the distribution of bead positions with a Gaussian function.
Calculate the trap stiffness k using the equation \(k = \frac{k_B T}{\sigma^2}\).
Prepare sample cells by placing a smaller cover slip on top of a bigger cover slip.
Separate the two cover slips with spacers approximately 200 μm high.
Cut a spacer from book wrapping foil measuring about 20×1 mm².
Glue together the sample cell closed on two opposite sides with spacers using UV curing glue.
Transfer the sample between the two cover slides to fill the sample cell with approximately 50 μl.
Seal the gaps between the slides on the opposite sides with silicone paste.
Place the sample cell under the microscope.
Generate two optical traps with a trap stiffness of approximately 1 pN/μm.
Trap a non-swimming bacterium in each of the traps.
Set the trapping plane at least 30 μm from bottom wall and at least 70 μm from the upper wall to minimize boundary effects.
Sinusoidally modulate the position of the optically trapped bacterium with a predefined frequency and amplitude.
Position the second optically trapped bacterium close to the active optical trap in the longitudinal direction, on the line connecting the two bacteria.
Record the positions of the two bacteria with a camera at approximately 50 frames per second or preferably at 200 frames per second.
Synchronize the camera image acquisition with trap movement using an external camera trigger.
Switch off the passive optical trap.
Allow the passive bacterium to follow the oscillations of the active trap.
Observe the correlated motion as soon as the bacterium is released from the passive trap.
When the passive bacterium drifts too far from the starting position, switch the passive trap on to reposition it.
Record the correlated motion of the two bacteria.
Incrementally increase distance between the two bacteria until you cannot observe the correlated motion anymore.
Acquire the position coordinates of the bacterial trajectories by analyzing recorded videos with particle tracking software.
Fit the measured trajectories with a sine function to determine the amplitude and frequency of the passive bacterium using data processing software that supports fitting of the sine function.
Set the limit of detection of the passive trap amplitude to at least 0.20 μm.
Determine the bacterial effective coupling distance.
Determine the coupling strength of bacterial pairs as a function of pair separation distance by comparing amplitude of passive bacterium oscillations at different distances.
Prepare bacterial culture as described in subsection A steps 1-4.
Prepare optical tweezers sample cell as described in subsection A step 6.
Calibrate optical tweezers as described in subsection A step 5.
Dilute 1 μl of the original bead suspension with a radius of 2.32 μm with Millipore water by a factor of 10^3 in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer 60 μl of diluted bead suspension to 1 ml of bacterial culture using pipette and mix.
Transfer 60 μl of diluted bead suspension to 1 ml of Millipore water using pipette and mix.
Transfer sample to the optical tweezer sample cell with a pipette.
Fill the sample cell with approximately 50 μl of sample.
Seal the gaps in the sample cell with a silicone paste to prevent evaporation of water and fluid currents.
Place the optical tweezer sample cell under the microscope.
Generate an optical trap with a trap stiffness of approximately 1 pN/μm using laser power no higher than a few 10 mW.
Trap a bead at least 20 μm from the sample cell wall to minimize boundary effects.
Sinusoidally modulate the position of the optical trap with a constant amplitude (e.g., 0.3 μm).
Modulate the trap position at different frequencies (0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 Hz).
Record the positions of measuring beads with a camera at no less than 50 frames per second.
Synchronize the camera image acquisition with trap movement using an external camera trigger to determine phase lag accurately between bacteria and trap positions.
Acquire the position coordinates of the bead trajectories in the sample and control.
Analyze recorded videos with particle tracking software.
Determine amplitude and phase lag of bead and laser-trap trajectories.
Obtain microrheological parameters of a sample and control.
Write the position of a sinusoidally modulated laser trap as x<sub>t</sub>\(t)=A<sub>t</sub>sin\(ωt).
Analyze recorded image stream to obtain particle position as x<sub>b</sub>\(t)=A<sub>b</sub>\(ω)sin\[ωt- δ<sub>b</sub>\(ω)].
Neglect inertial term and thermal fluctuations in the equation of motion for the spherical probe x\(t).
Solve equations of motion to give both components of a complex viscoelastic modulus: G'\(ω).
Grow bacteria in SM medium or M9 medium with low polymeric background for TEM.
Collect bacterial samples at different times during incubation.
Transfer approximately 20 μl of bacterial culture onto grids covered with Formvar support film.
Incubate the grid with bacteria for 5 minutes to allow attachment.
Remove excess medium by touching filter paper gently against the edge of the grid.
Negatively stain the samples by transferring approximately 20 μl of 1% (w/v) aqueous uranyl acetate over the grids.
Incubate the stained sample on the grid for 5 seconds.
Carefully remove contrasting medium using filter paper and let the sample dry in air.
Examine the dried samples under TEM at 80 keV.
Collect samples of the bacterial culture in microcentrifuge tubes.
Fix the samples in 1% (v/v) formaldehyde and 0.5% (v/v) glutaraldehyde in a 0.1 M cacodylate buffer for at least 20 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer approximately 100 μl of fixed samples to pre-cleaned glass slides.
Rinse the slides in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Postfix attached cells and extracellular matrix in a 1% (v/v) aqueous solution of osmium tetroxide for 1 hour at 4°C.
Rinse the slides with deionized water.
Dehydrate samples in ethanol series (50, 70, 90, 96, and 100% (v/v)) for 5 minutes each.
Transfer dehydrated samples to acetone.
Gradually replace acetone with hexamethyldisilazane through a series of 30%, 60%, and 100% (v/v) in absolute acetone.
Air dry the slides.
Attach slides to metal holders.
Sputter-coat the samples with a 5 nm layer of platinum.
Examine samples with SEM.
Culture bacteria in a liquid medium with low fluorescent background.
Collect approximately 100 μl of bacterial culture sample at selected incubation times for fluorescent microscopy.
Prepare TOTO-1 iodide nucleic acid stain stock solution by diluting the original concentrate 10-fold in PBS to achieve a final concentration of 2 μM.
Add 2 μl of TOTO-1 stock solution to 50 μl of bacterial culture and gently mix.
Transfer 10 μl of the mixture to a microscope glass slide.
Cover the slide with a cover slide and seal the gap using a preheated mixture of non-bleaching vaseline, paraffin, and lanolin.
Immediately observe the prepared samples using a fluorescence microscope equipped with a mercury lamp and appropriate objectives and filters.
Record images with a coupled camera.
Coat the wells of diagnostic slides by transferring approximately 10 µl of 0.05 % (w/v) poly L-lysine into each well.
Wait approximately an hour at room temperature until water evaporates.
Grow the strain expressing fluorescently labeled target protein in a liquid medium.
Collect approximately 1 ml of culture samples of labeled and unlabeled strains at selected time intervals.
Centrifuge the cultures at 10,000×g for 10 min to separate cells from the liquid medium.
Replace the supernatant with an equal volume of phosphate-buffered saline solution (PBS).
Transfer approximately 15 µl of cell suspension to each coated well and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Rinse with PBS to remove unattached cells and disperse excess fluid.
Add 2 µl of SlowFade Gold antifade reagent to each well to reduce photo-bleaching of the marker.
Cover the slides with cover slides (60×24 mm², #1.5).
Examine the slides with the fluorescence microscope.
Record differential interference contrast (DIC) images of the view fields.
Record fluorescence (FL) images of the same view fields.
Analyze the obtained images using Fiji (ImageJ) software script.
Enable the Split channels option in the Bio-formats Import Options menu.
Make an average fluoresceinate image from two standard solution images taken at the beginning and end of the session.
Remove local impurities from the standard images.
Convert the DIC sample image to a binary image.
Normalize the FL sample image to the fluorescein standard.
Subtract the background from the FL image.
Multiply normalized, background and flat-field corrected FL image by the binary image obtained from DIC.
Obtain mean fluorescence intensity of each individual cell.
Save results as an excel spreadsheet, with each line corresponding to one object (cell).
Save corrected and extracted images to the chosen directory.
Determine population distributions in fluorescent marker expression using OriginPro software.
Measure individual cells fluorescence with microscopy.
